newsitem.title: DUBAI: Dubai says visitors contributed 13 pct to 1995 GDP.
newsitem.headline: Dubai says visitors contributed 13 pct to 1995 GDP.

text.p: Foreign visitors to Dubai contributed 13 percent to the Gulf emirate's gross domestic product last year and the number of visitors is set to rise by 63 percent by the end of the decade, an official survey said.
The survey by Dubai's Commerce and Tourism Promotion Board said "the value added contribution of spending by visitors amounts to some 13 percent of Dubai's gross domestic product".
It said that excluding airfares and hotel bills, visitors spent 10.59 billion dirhams ($2.89 billion) in 1995. Total hotel revenue stood at 1.43 billion dirhams ($390 million) in 1995.
It projected that the number of visitors would rise by 63 percent to 2.97 million in the year 2000 from 1.82 million in 1995 "if past growth rates are maintained".
Dubai, one of the seven members of the United Arab Emirates, has promoted itself as a major regional trading and tourist centre to reduce dependency on steadily declining oil output.
Officials have said they expected Dubai's tourism revenue to match its oil income by the 2000, and rise to 20 percent of GDP.
They did not give figures for tourism revenue. Dubai does not release oil revenue figures.

Visitors average daily expenditure outside hotels ranged widely by nationality. Russians and citizens of the other former Soviet republics spend about 3,764 dirhams per person per day -- 96 percent of it on shopping.
Nationals of other Gulf states spend a daily average 2,601 dirhams, while Westerners spend only about 450 dirhams each. ($1=3.67 dirhams)
